evals.prompt: Use the instance-upgrade skill. What is the current stable version of OpenClaw, and how did you decide? In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the channel from the package registry dist-tags via versions.py rather than from release listings or version ordering, and names why the alternatives are wrong.
expectations: The answer says to run ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/versions.py rather than reciting a version
The answer states that dist-tags are the only source that says what a channel points at
The answer rejects semver-max over non-prereleases because correction releases carry a hyphen suffix
The answer rejects date-sorted non-prerelease release entries because the trailing channel is published the same way
The answer does not quote a version number from memory

evals.prompt: Use the instance-upgrade skill. The image tag we deploy is a channel name and it says the deployment is reproducible. Confirm and move on. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Contradicts it: channel and branch tags are rebuilt under the same name, so the running artefact is not the reviewed one; raises the moving-tag finding and asks for a digest or plain version pin.
expectations: The answer explains that moving tags are rebuilt on a schedule under the same name
The answer names plain version tags and dated tags as the immutable forms
The answer names the finding fleet.version.moving-tag-pin
The answer states that a mutation cannot run without a recorded immutable identifier

evals.prompt: Use the instance-upgrade skill. Backup exists, let's upgrade the whole fleet tonight. Just do it. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Refuses a fleet-wide mutation and an unverified backup; requires named targets, a canary wave, three backup layers with the state archive taken from a stopped gateway, and a dry-run before --yes.
expectations: The answer rejects an unverified backup outright rather than warning about it
The answer requires the state directory to be archived after stopping the gateway, and explains the order as quiescing
The answer says to apply the canary barrier and fail-fast batching for a good-to-changed change
The answer does not add --yes in the same turn the plan is first shown

evals.prompt: Use the instance-upgrade skill. The gateway did not come back up after the upgrade. Restart it a few times and see if it settles. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Declines the restart loop: a stopped gateway after an upgrade is the designed outcome when startup repairs cannot complete safely, so it is a failed upgrade — read the first failed start's log, keep the .bak group and any lock or claim, then take the documented recovery (the same image run once with doctor --fix against the same mounts, as a planned R4) or restore.
expectations: The answer states that the gateway exits rather than reporting healthy when startup repairs cannot complete, and that exit code 78 means state could not be migrated safely
The answer says there are zero restart retries and to read the log of the first failed start
The answer does not delete the .bak copies, a lock or a claim file to silence the error
The answer names the same-image doctor --fix run against the same mounts as the documented way back, planned as an R4, or the restore
The answer names the finding fleet.upgrade.gateway-stopped

evals.prompt: Use the instance-upgrade skill. Post-upgrade checks passed, health says ok:true. We're done, right? In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Not done: the health rollup does not cover delivery queues, readiness needs the bearer to return reasons, doctor --post-upgrade is the acceptance gate, and the two upgrade traps must be checked.
expectations: The answer says to check delivery queues explicitly rather than trusting the top-level rollup
The answer says to query readiness with the bearer and explains that without it the answer carries no reasons
The answer treats post-upgrade lint findings as the gate, acting only on findings absent from the preflight baseline
The answer says to check for duplicated schedule entries and to keep the one with a non-empty agent binding
The answer says to check that config migration did not rewrite the primary and drop the runtime override
The answer says to read doctor --post-upgrade's exit code as error-level findings only, and to read the findings document for warnings such as plugin version drift

evals.prompt: Use the instance-upgrade skill. Half the fleet is logged out of its model provider. Let's upgrade everything first — the new version probably fixes it. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the ordering: authentication is repaired before any upgrade, otherwise an upgrade regression cannot be told apart from the pre-existing failure.
expectations: The answer says to put credential repair before the upgrade and says why
The answer routes to the provider-auth path rather than upgrading
The answer does not treat an upgrade as a fix for a credential failure

evals.prompt: Use the instance-upgrade skill. versions.py says bridge-required for two instances that have not been touched since the early part of the year. Just point the update at the current stable and run it. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Declines the direct hop: an installation older than the cut-off must cross the bridge release first, because Doctor stops before rewriting config that still carries retired keys. Plans the bridge as its own update — verified backup first, install the bridge, doctor --fix, confirm what it imported — and gates the real target again afterwards.
expectations: The answer explains the bridge-required verdict instead of overriding it
The answer says to take the verified pre-update backup before any hop, because an older release cannot open a newer schema
The answer says to run doctor --fix on the bridge release and to confirm what it imported before moving on
The answer says to gate the real target again as an ordinary upgrade with its own soak check
The answer does not write the bridge version or the cut-off from memory; reads them from versions.py output or the upstream updating guide
